rv.q: The result at Northlight is a modestly entertaining piece of theater — it’s only 70 minutes — that falls somewhat short of riveting real-time drama (you don’t really believe Warhol is in any danger) but debates a lot of interesting cultural history.
There's a rare, ineffable alchemy when acting prowess and charisma merge into something unforgettable. That's what Dehghani brings to the stage.
If you see only one play this season, you are advised to head straight to Northlight Theatre for “Andy Warhol in Iran,” a riveting, brilliantly imagined two-character work...
Adding a touch of sarcastic humor, Lindley and Dehghani kept the audience engaged with this brilliant storyline of pain and purpose.
Lindley's crisp, clever and measured approach that pours out and will ignite the inevitable conversation about Warhol's vast complexity.
Northlight’s production of ‘Andy Warhol in Tehran’ is a unique expression from those who know, and comes highly recommended.
Askari's play is a highly watchable and often quite funny piece.
In this entertaining and enlightening 70-minute dramedy we learn new information or are reminded about the details of Andy Warhol’s life.
Rob Lindley as Warhol is an unwavering glimpse of a man oscillating around a jaded moral compass.
This is probably one of the best 81 minutes of theater you can have.
Andy Warhol in Iran is one of the best productions of theater that I have seen in the past year.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically praise this riveting two-hander as an incisive, thought-provoking exploration of art, politics, and revolution, with particular acclaim for Rob Lindley's precise portrayal of Warhol and Brent Askari's sharp, witty writing.
